Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the IDD disclosure content set (IPID, demands-and-needs statement, distributor status and remuneration disclosure, IBIP costs-and-charges) built into each EEA product's form and correspondence library; escalates drafting disputes to Regulatory Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - IDD (EU) 2016/97 Arts. 17(1), 18, 19, 20(1)-(8), 23, 29(1)-(2) and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1469 (IPID standardised presentation format) re-read on EUR-Lex at each product change, together with the national transposition text of every EEA host state the product is passported into

In-scope processes.value: Product design and change intake -> disclosure build -> POG target-market sign-off -> form and template release, for every EEA non-life IPID, life pre-contract pack and IBIP costs-and-charges schedule, plus quote, renewal and mid-term-adjustment correspondence carrying the same wording

In-scope systems.value: Document template library and correspondence engine in the policy administration platform, feeding the customer portal and broker portal; approved master PDFs held in the document management repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: IDD Disclosure Build Procedure - one row per disclosure obligation (Art. 18 distributor identity and register number, Art. 19 fee/commission nature, Art. 20(1) demands and needs, Art. 20(4)-(8) IPID, Art. 29 IBIP costs and charges), naming the form, the trigger point and the responsible template owner

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the product oversight and governance (POG) committee; re-approved on every product change and at least annually against new EIOPA guidance and host-state conduct rules

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per change - no EEA product may be released for distribution until its IPID and pre-contract pack are approved; the disclosure set is re-reviewed at the annual POG product review and within 30 days of any national transposition amendment

Deadline reminders configured.value: Form inventory alerts at product-freeze minus 45 days and minus 15 days for unapproved disclosure templates, plus a standing annual POG review reminder per product and a regulatory-change alert on the EIOPA and host-NCA bulletin feeds

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Form inventory extract, dated IPID drafts with the Art. 20(8) two-sided-A4 layout check, translation certificates and POG approval minutes retained for the life of the contract plus 10 years

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any EEA product distributed with a missing, superseded or untranslated IDD disclosure is raised as a conduct exception with root cause, affected policy count and a customer-remediation decision

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs off every IPID wording change, every host-state language variant and every decision not to re-issue disclosures to already-sold policies

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every EEA product version live in the period per the form inventory, cut by product, host state, language and distribution channel, joined to the templates actually rendered by the correspondence engine

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on missing mandatory content - any product distributed without a current IPID, demands-and-needs statement or remuneration disclosure fails; a single fail escalates to the POG committee and the Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per product change; the test runs on 100% of products changed in the quarter plus an annual full sweep of the EEA form inventory ahead of the POG annual review

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have drafted, translated or approved any sampled disclosure template

Evidence location for test results.value: IDD disclosure content workpaper (form inventory extract, per-product content matrix, rendered specimen packs, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under the product and version

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Form inventory export with product, host state, language, template version and effective dates, plus specimen packs, presentable to a host NCA or EIOPA thematic review within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Distribution Compliance owns the host-NCA response through the home-state supervisor under IDD Art. 5 cooperation; Regulatory Counsel clears any admission that a disclosure was omitted before it leaves the building

checklist.step: Open the disclosure build record for the product change
actions: Take the approved product change from the POG intake queue and record product name, underwriting entity, EEA home state, every host state under freedom of services or establishment, and the target launch date.
Ask the Head of Distribution which channels will sell it (direct, tied agent, broker, comparison site, embedded partner) - each channel drives a different Art. 18 status disclosure.
Classify the product as non-life (IPID required, Art. 20(4)), life non-IBIP, or insurance-based investment product (Art. 29 costs and charges plus Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 applies).
Open a disclosure build record and attach the signed change request and the draft target market statement.
checklist.done: the build record names product, entity, home and host states, channels and product classification, with the change request attached.

checklist.step: List every IDD disclosure the product must carry
actions: Add one row per obligation: Art. 18(a)-(b) identity, address, register entry and register-check method; Art. 19(1) nature of remuneration (fee, commission, other) and whether advice is on a fair and personal analysis; Art. 20(1) demands-and-needs statement; Art. 20(4)-(8) IPID; Art. 22 cross-selling; Art. 29(1)-(2) IBIP costs and charges and periodic reporting.
For each row name the document that will carry it (IPID, pre-contract pack, quote letter, statement of demands and needs, key features document) and the trigger point in the journey.
Mark rows that only apply to a channel (for example the Art. 19(1)(c) broker fair-and-personal-analysis statement) so tied-agent journeys are not over-disclosed.
Send the matrix to Regulatory Counsel for a completeness read before drafting starts.
checklist.done: every IDD article in scope has a row naming the carrying document, the trigger point and the applicable channels.

checklist.step: Check the national transposition for each host state on top of the Directive
actions: For each host state open the transposing text (for example Germany VVG and VersVermV, France Code des assurances L.521-1 et seq., Ireland Central Bank Consumer Protection Code) and read the gold-plating on top of Arts. 18-20.
Record every host-state add-on: extra pre-contract statements, prescribed font or ordering, mandatory ombudsman naming, local complaints-body address.
Confirm the language requirement under Art. 23(1) - the official language of the member state of the commitment unless the customer and distributor agree otherwise.
Write the add-ons onto the matrix rows as sub-requirements with the local citation and its effective date.
checklist.done: each host state has a documented add-on list with local citations, or an explicit 'no gold-plating' note signed by counsel.

checklist.step: Draft the IPID in the prescribed standardised format
actions: Build the IPID against Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1469: title 'Insurance Product Information Document', the company name, member state of registration and regulatory status immediately under it, and the standard section headings with their prescribed icons.

Complete each section in short bullets - 'What is this type of insurance?', 'What is insured?', 'What is not insured?', 'Are there any restrictions on cover?', 'Where am I covered?', 'What are my obligations?', 'When and how do I pay?', 'When does the cover start and end?', 'How do I cancel the contract?'.
Keep the document to two sides of A4 when printed, three only where the Implementing Regulation permits, and check it in print preview rather than on screen.
Pull the What-is-insured and What-is-not-insured content from the approved policy wording rather than marketing copy, and cite the wording clause number in the drafting notes.
Save the draft into the document management repository as <product>-IPID-<host state>-v<n>.
checklist.done: the IPID follows the Implementing Regulation layout, fits the page limit in print, and every statement traces to a policy wording clause.

checklist.step: Draft the distributor status and remuneration disclosure per channel
actions: Write the Art. 18 block: legal name, address, whether the firm is an insurance undertaking or intermediary, the register in which it is entered with the registration number, and how the customer can verify the entry.

Write the Art. 19(1) remuneration block per channel: employee salary, fee paid by the customer, commission included in the premium, or another arrangement - stating the type, not merely that remuneration exists.

Add the Art. 19(1)(c) statement of whether advice is given on the basis of a fair and personal analysis, and where a broker is not, name the undertakings the firm places business with or state that the list is available on request.
Add the complaints route and the out-of-court redress body required by Art. 18(b)(vi) and Art. 15, naming the host-state ombudsman.
Circulate the per-channel blocks to the Head of Broker Distribution to confirm they describe the real commercial arrangements.
checklist.done: each channel has an Art. 18/19 block naming the register entry, the remuneration type and the host-state redress body, confirmed as commercially accurate.

checklist.step: Draft the demands-and-needs statement and the advice wording
actions: Draft the Art. 20(1) demands-and-needs statement so the proposed contract is expressly stated to be consistent with the customer's demands and needs, with the captured answers reproduced back to the customer.
Where advice is given, draft the personalised recommendation wording required by Art. 20(1) sub-paragraph 3 - an explanation of why a particular product best meets the customer's demands and needs.
For IBIPs add the Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Art. 9 suitability content, including the sustainability-preferences question set required since 2 August 2022 under Regulation (EU) 2021/1257.
Write the non-advised variant so it cannot be read as a recommendation, and have Regulatory Counsel confirm the boundary.
checklist.done: advised and non-advised wording variants exist, each carrying a demands-and-needs statement, with counsel confirmation on the advice boundary.

checklist.step: Draft the IBIP costs and charges disclosure
actions: For IBIPs build the Art. 29(1)(c) aggregated costs and charges disclosure: all costs of distribution and of the product, including the cost of advice, the cost of the underlying investment and how the customer may pay for it.
Show the aggregate figure in cash and as a percentage, and add the cumulative effect on return illustration required by Art. 29(1)(c).
Reconcile the cost inputs to the fund charge schedule from Investment Operations and the commission schedule from the billing/commission platform before the figure is fixed.
State the Art. 29(2) commitment to provide the information at least annually during the life of the contract.
checklist.done: the IBIP pack shows aggregated costs in cash and percentage, a cumulative-effect illustration, and reconciles to the fund and commission schedules.

checklist.step: Run the fair, clear and not misleading review over the whole pack
actions: Read the full pack against Art. 17(1) - honest, fair and professional conduct in the best interests of customers - and Art. 17(2) fair, clear and not misleading marketing communications.
Strike any exclusion buried below a benefit statement, any 'subject to terms' qualifier without the term, and any figure without its basis.
Run a readability pass and record the score used, targeting plain language at the target market described in the POG statement.
Log each challenge and its resolution on the review sheet so the drafting decisions are auditable.
checklist.done: a signed review sheet shows every fair-clear-not-misleading challenge and its resolution against Art. 17.

checklist.step: Translate and localise for each host state
actions: Send the approved source pack to the certified translation vendor with a glossary of the prescribed IPID headings so the mandated wording is not paraphrased.
Require a back-translation for the IPID and the demands-and-needs statement and compare it line by line to the source.
Re-check the two-sided-A4 limit after translation - German and Finnish text expansion routinely breaks the layout.
Have the host-state legal contact confirm the local ombudsman name, address and register wording in the translated version.
File the translation certificate with the language variant in the document management repository.
checklist.done: each host-state language variant has a back-translation check, a page-limit re-check and a filed translation certificate.

checklist.step: Build the approved wording into templates and correspondence
actions: Raise a template change request naming each approved document, its version, the host states and languages it serves, and the journey trigger that must render it.
Map every merge field the pack needs - register number, remuneration type, intermediary name, aggregate cost figure - to a system data element rather than hard-coded text.
Bind the IPID and pre-contract pack to the quote-issue event so they cannot be skipped, and bind the IBIP annual costs statement to the anniversary job.
Hand the mapping to the Configuration Engineer with the specimen pack attached as the rendering target.
checklist.done: every approved document is bound to a journey trigger with data-driven merge fields and a specimen rendering target.

checklist.step: Proof the rendered output for every product, state and channel combination
actions: Generate test quotes covering each product, host state, language and channel and render the full pack in the correspondence engine.
Compare each rendered document to the approved specimen field by field, including register number, remuneration wording, ombudsman address and cost figures.
Check the PDF renders inside the page limit, that no merge field prints as a placeholder, and that the pack is complete on both the portal and the print stream.
Log defects to the template change request and re-render after fix - never sign off on a corrected screenshot.
checklist.done: every product/state/channel combination renders a complete pack matching the approved specimen, with all defects closed by re-render.

checklist.step: Get POG and counsel approval before release
actions: Present the disclosure matrix, specimen packs and QA evidence to the POG committee with the target market statement.
Obtain Regulatory Counsel written approval on the IPID wording and on every host-state language variant.
Record the committee decision, the approved template versions and the effective date in the minutes.
Release the templates only after both approvals are recorded - a conditional approval keeps the product gated.
checklist.done: POG minutes and a counsel approval record name the exact template versions approved and the release date.

checklist.step: Update the form inventory as the single record of what is in use
actions: Add or update one inventory row per document: product, underwriting entity, host state, language, document type, template version, IDD article satisfied, effective from and effective to.
Retire the superseded version by setting its effective-to date rather than deleting it, so historic sales can be evidenced.
Link each row to the approved master PDF, the POG minute and the counsel approval.
Reconcile the inventory to the template list actually deployed in the policy administration platform and clear any difference the same week.
checklist.done: the form inventory reconciles to deployed templates and every row links to a master PDF, POG minute and counsel approval.

checklist.step: Brief distribution partners on what changed and when it applies
actions: Publish the new pack and a one-page change summary to the broker and agent portal with the go-live date.
Instruct partners in writing to destroy or archive the superseded IPID and pre-contract pack and confirm receipt.
Where partners generate their own quote documentation, require written confirmation that their own templates now carry the updated Art. 18/19 blocks.
Chase non-confirming partners through the Agency Relations Manager and suspend new business where confirmation is not received by go-live.
checklist.done: every active distribution partner has confirmed receipt of the new pack and withdrawal of the superseded version.

checklist.step: File the evidence and set the review cycle
actions: File the disclosure matrix, drafts, translation certificates, QA renderings, POG minutes and counsel approvals under the product and version.
Apply the contract-life-plus-10-years retention label so the pack survives product withdrawal.
Schedule the annual POG disclosure review and register the product on the EIOPA and host-NCA regulatory-change watchlist.
Confirm the repository index makes the record searchable by product, host state, language and IDD article.
checklist.done: the disclosure evidence set is filed, retention-labelled, watch-listed and searchable by product, state and IDD article.

testing.step: Build the population of EEA product versions distributed in the period
actions: Extract from the form inventory every document row with an effective-from or effective-to date inside the period, by product, underwriting entity, host state, language and channel.
Add every product that recorded new business in an EEA state during the period from the policy administration new-business extract, so a product with no inventory row cannot hide.
Reconcile the two counts and resolve every product present in sales but absent from the inventory before sampling.
testing.done: the population reconciles the form inventory to EEA new-business activity and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the inventory to the templates actually deployed
actions: Pull the deployed template list with version numbers and activation dates from the correspondence engine configuration.
Match it to the form inventory on product, host state, language and version and list every deployed template with no inventory row and every inventory row with no deployed template.
Treat any deployed template that never passed POG approval as an automatic exception regardless of its content quality.
testing.done: every deployed template matches an approved inventory row, or the difference is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample across products, states and channels
actions: Take 100% of IBIP products and 100% of products launched into a new host state during the period.
Take 20 further product/state/channel combinations by seeded random selection from the remainder, minimum 35 rows in total.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and stratification in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all IBIPs and all new host-state launches, and its method is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the content check against the Directive and the Implementing Regulation
actions: Open the current EUR-Lex text of IDD Arts. 18, 19, 20 and 29 and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1469 and build your own required-content list before looking at the firm's matrix.
Read each sampled specimen pack and tick or fail each required element - register number, remuneration type, fair-and-personal-analysis statement, demands-and-needs statement, IBIP aggregate cost.
Check the IPID layout against the Implementing Regulation: title, status line, prescribed headings, icons and the two-sided-A4 print limit.
Record a fail for a right element in the wrong document as well as for a missing element.
testing.done: each sampled pack carries an independent element-by-element content conclusion referenced to the source text.

testing.step: Test the host-state add-ons and language variants
actions: For each sampled host state read the transposing national text as it stood on the template effective date and list the local add-ons.
Check the language variant carries every add-on, names the correct local ombudsman and complaints body, and is in the language of the member state of the commitment per Art. 23(1).
Read the back-translation of the IPID headings and fail any paraphrase of the prescribed wording.
Confirm a translation certificate exists and is dated before the template went live.
testing.done: every sampled host state variant is verified against national transposition, local redress bodies and a pre-dated translation certificate.

testing.step: Re-render the pack from the live system and compare to the approved master
actions: Generate a live test quote for each sampled product/state/channel and render the full pre-contract pack.
Compare the rendered document to the approved master PDF held in the document management repository field by field.
Fail any placeholder merge field, truncated page, missing document or stale version rendered in place of the approved one.
Capture the rendered PDFs into the workpaper as the evidence of what the customer actually receives.
testing.done: each sampled combination renders the approved master with no placeholder, truncation or version drift, evidenced by a captured PDF.

testing.step: Trace sold policies back to the disclosure version in force
actions: Select five policies sold under each sampled product/state combination and pull the archived pre-contract documents attached to each policy record.
Compare the archived template version and issue timestamp to the inventory effective-from and effective-to dates.
Flag any policy issued in a version gap - superseded pack still in use, or the new pack used before its approval date.
Record the policy number, template version and timestamp for every traced item.
testing.done: every traced policy carries an archived pack whose version was approved and in force at the sale date.

testing.step: Recompute the IBIP costs-and-charges figures
actions: For each sampled IBIP recompute the Art. 29(1)(c) aggregate cost from the fund charge schedule, the product charge table and the commission schedule in the billing/commission platform.
Compare the recomputed cash and percentage figures to the printed disclosure and record any difference above 0.05 percentage points as an exception.
Re-run the cumulative-effect-on-return illustration on the disclosed assumptions and check the assumptions themselves are stated in the pack.
Confirm the pack states the Art. 29(2) annual reporting commitment.
testing.done: disclosed IBIP costs reconcile to source charge and commission schedules within tolerance and the illustration is reproducible.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and customer impact
actions: Raise one issue per exception with product, host state, template version, the IDD article breached and the count of policies sold on the defective pack.
Assign a root cause (matrix missed an article, translation drift, template deployed without POG approval, host-state add-on not tracked) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and, where customers received a defective IPID or remuneration disclosure, open a re-issue and host-NCA notification assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with root cause, owner, affected policy count, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate by product and by host state and compare it to the zero-tolerance threshold on missing mandatory content.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted, translated or approved none of the sampled templates, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any customer-impacting defect to the POG committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, per-state exception rate and a POG reporting date is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Define the trigger-to-document map for every journey
actions: List every event that triggers an IDD document: quote issue, application submission, contract conclusion, mid-term adjustment, renewal invitation, IBIP anniversary, cancellation.
Against each event name the document set from the approved form inventory and the host states and languages it applies to.

Record the required timing for each - pre-contract pack in good time before conclusion under Art. 20(5), renewal invitation at the host-state lead time, IBIP annual statement within 30 days of anniversary.
Get Compliance to confirm the map covers every product type, including IBIPs and cross-sold packages under Art. 22.
checklist.done: every trigger event maps to a named document set, host state list and a stated timing rule confirmed by Compliance.

checklist.step: Set and document the 'in good time' standard the firm will operate
actions: Convert the Art. 20(5) 'in good time before the conclusion' obligation into an operating rule per channel - for example pack despatched at quote and at least 24 hours before conclusion for digital journeys, at point of quote for face-to-face.
Document the telephone-sale route under Art. 23(6): limited information by voice with the full pack on a durable medium immediately after conclusion, plus the distance-marketing information duties.

Record the durable-medium decision tree from Art. 23(2)-(5): paper by default, other durable medium or website only where the appropriateness test, the customer's choice and the e-mail address evidence are captured.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm the standard is defensible in each host state and record the sign-off date.
checklist.done: a written, counsel-approved timing and durable-medium standard exists per channel and host state.

checklist.step: Capture and store the customer's durable-medium and language choice
actions: At application, capture the customer's delivery preference and, for non-paper delivery, the evidence of regular internet access required by Art. 23(5) and a valid e-mail address.
Store the preference, the consent timestamp and the language choice on the policy record as reportable fields, not as free-text notes.
Default any record with missing or invalid contact data to paper delivery rather than suppressing the document.
Expose the standing Art. 23(4) right to request a paper copy free of charge in the pack and in the portal, routed to the correspondence queue.
checklist.done: every policy carries a stored delivery preference, consent timestamp and language, with paper as the fallback.

checklist.step: Generate the document set on the trigger event
actions: Let the event fire the correspondence job and confirm it selects the template version in force for the product, host state, language and channel on that date.
Check the generated set is complete against the trigger-to-document map - a partial pack is a failed generation, not a partial success.
Write a notice-log row per document with document id, policy, trigger event, template version, generation timestamp and intended channel.
Send generation failures to the daily exception queue with the failing policy and reason code rather than silently retrying.
checklist.done: each trigger produces a complete, correctly versioned document set with a notice-log row, or a logged generation failure.

checklist.step: Despatch through the customer's chosen channel and record proof
actions: Release the print stream to the mail vendor with the daily manifest, or send the e-mail with the pack attached, or publish to the customer portal with an out-of-band notification.
Record the despatch timestamp, channel and a proof reference - mail vendor manifest id, e-mail message id and delivery receipt, or portal publication id and first-view timestamp.
Reconcile the mail vendor's daily acceptance file to the manifest and chase any document the vendor did not accept the same day.
Update the notice-log row status to Despatched, Bounced or Failed with the reason code.
checklist.done: every generated document has a despatch timestamp, channel, proof reference and a status reconciled to the vendor acceptance file.

checklist.step: Block conclusion where the pre-contract pack has not gone out
actions: Configure the bind/issue step to check for a Despatched pre-contract pack for that quote before the contract can be concluded.
Where the pack is missing or failed, stop the transaction and route the case to the correspondence queue rather than allowing an override.
Where a business override is unavoidable, force a reason code, a named approver at manager grade and an automatic conduct-exception record.
Report all overrides weekly to Compliance with the policy number and the approver.
checklist.done: conclusion is system-blocked without a despatched pre-contract pack, and every override is reason-coded, approved and reported.

checklist.step: Run the daily undelivered and failed-delivery queue
actions: Work the daily queue of bounced e-mails, returned mail, failed portal publications and generation errors, oldest first.
Correct the contact data against the source of record, or switch the policy to paper, and re-issue the document the same working day.
Where the customer cannot be reached after two attempts, raise a case to Consumer Affairs for tracing rather than closing the item as undeliverable.
Record the re-issue date and the new proof reference against the original notice-log row so the delay is visible.
checklist.done: the queue is cleared daily, every failure has a re-issue or a traced case, and delays remain visible on the original log row.

checklist.step: Despatch renewal invitations at the host-state lead time
actions: Run the renewal invitation job against the host-state lead time held on the product record, backing off the renewal date.
Confirm the invitation carries the updated IPID where the product has changed and the Art. 20 demands-and-needs restatement where required at renewal.
Review the aging report daily and escalate any invitation not despatched by the statutory lead date to the Policy Admin Ops Lead before the renewal date passes.
Where the lead time has been missed, extend cover on the existing terms rather than auto-renewing on undisclosed new terms, and log the decision.
checklist.done: every renewal invitation is despatched by the host-state lead date or has an escalated, logged decision protecting the customer.

checklist.step: Produce the IBIP annual costs and suitability statements
actions: Run the anniversary-minus-10-working-days job to list IBIP policies due their Art. 29(2) annual costs and charges statement.
Pull the year's actual costs from the billing/commission platform and the fund charge feed rather than re-printing the point-of-sale illustration.
Where advice was given, include the periodic suitability statement required by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Art. 18, restating why the product remains suitable.
Despatch within 30 days of the anniversary and record the despatch proof against the policy.
checklist.done: every IBIP receives an annual costs statement built on actual costs, with a suitability statement where advised, despatched within 30 days of anniversary.

checklist.step: Archive every despatched document against the policy
actions: Write the rendered PDF into the archive keyed by policy number, document type, template version and despatch timestamp.
Apply the contract-life-plus-10-years retention label and set the record to immutable so a later template change cannot rewrite history.
Confirm the archived copy is byte-identical to what was despatched by checksum, not by re-rendering from the current template.
Expose the archive to Consumer Affairs and Complaints so a customer file can be assembled without an IT request.
checklist.done: every despatched document is archived immutably, checksum-matched to the despatched copy and retrievable by policy number.

checklist.step: Serve paper-copy and language requests within five business days
actions: Log every Art. 23(4) free paper copy request and every request for a different official language as a case with the requested documents listed.
Order the reprint from the archive, not a fresh render, so the customer receives what was originally issued.
Despatch within 5 business days at no charge and record the despatch proof on the case.
Update the policy delivery preference to paper where the customer asks for future documents on paper.
checklist.done: every paper or language request is despatched free within 5 business days from the archived copy, with proof on the case.

checklist.step: Monitor the delivery service levels weekly
actions: Publish a weekly dashboard: pre-contract packs despatched before conclusion, renewal invitations inside the statutory lead time, IBIP statements inside 30 days, and open failures by age.
Break the numbers by host state, channel and product so a single broker portal or print vendor problem is visible.
Set a red threshold at any pre-contract pack despatched after conclusion and at renewal timeliness below 99%.
Take red items to the daily operations stand-up with a named owner and a fix date.
checklist.done: a weekly dashboard by state, channel and product exists and every red item carries an owner and a fix date.

checklist.step: Handle vendor and channel outages without dropping documents
actions: Hold a written fallback per channel: alternate print vendor, secondary e-mail relay, and a manual despatch route for the pre-contract pack.
On an outage, freeze conclusion for affected journeys rather than concluding contracts without the pack.
Rebuild the missed queue from the notice log once service returns and re-despatch in event order, oldest first.
Record the outage window, the affected document count and the recovery completion time in the incident record.
checklist.done: each outage has a recorded window, an affected document count, a completed catch-up despatch and no contract concluded without its pack.

checklist.step: Assess customer detriment on every late or missed pack
actions: For each pack despatched after conclusion, check whether the customer had the information needed to exercise the withdrawal or cancellation right and whether the period should be restarted.
Where cover terms differed from what was disclosed, calculate the customer's position and propose redress before the customer complains.
Refer any cluster affecting more than 50 policies to the Compliance Manager for a host-NCA notification assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Record the assessment, the decision and the redress on the exception case.
checklist.done: every late or missed pack has a documented detriment assessment, a redress decision and a notification assessment where clustered.

checklist.step: File the monthly delivery evidence pack
actions: Assemble the month's notice-log extract, exception queue closure statistics, override list and detriment assessments.
File under the reporting month with the contract-life-plus-10-years retention label.
Confirm the extract can be filtered by policy number, host state, trigger event and delivery status for a regulator or ombudsman request.
Hand the pack to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for the quarterly conduct risk report.
checklist.done: a filtered, retention-labelled monthly delivery evidence pack is filed and handed to conduct risk reporting.

testing.step: Build the population of IDD trigger events for the month
actions: Extract every contract conclusion, renewal, mid-term adjustment and IBIP anniversary dated in the month from the policy administration event log, by host state, product and channel.
Include broker-bound and embedded-partner business, which often posts on a delayed feed and is missed by a same-day extract.
Reconcile the conclusion count to the new-business production report and resolve any difference before sampling.
testing.done: the event population reconciles to the production report and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Join events to the notice log and expose the gaps
actions: Left-join every trigger event to the notice log on policy and event id and list events with no document row at all.
Compare the documents generated against the trigger-to-document map and list every incomplete set.
Treat any concluded contract with no despatched pre-contract pack as an automatic exception with no sampling judgement applied.
testing.done: every trigger event is matched to a complete despatched document set or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Recompute the timing against the Art. 20(5) and host-state deadlines
actions: Compute despatch timestamp minus conclusion timestamp for every pre-contract pack and flag every non-negative result.

Compute renewal invitation despatch date against the renewal date and compare to the host-state lead time held on the product record - re-derive the lead time from the transposition text rather than trusting the field.
Compute IBIP statement despatch minus anniversary date and flag anything over 30 days.
Reconcile the computed timeliness percentages to the operational dashboard and explain any difference.
testing.done: timing is independently recomputed for every population row and reconciles to the reported dashboard figures.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample weighted to the risk
actions: Take 100% of packs despatched at or after conclusion and 100% of overrides recorded at the bind step.
Take 25 timely items by seeded random selection across host states and channels to test that recorded timeliness is real.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, includes every late pack and override, and its method is documented.

testing.step: Trace each sampled item to its proof of despatch
actions: Open the notice-log row and follow the proof reference to the mail vendor manifest line, the e-mail delivery receipt or the portal publication and first-view record.
Confirm the proof names the same policy, document type and date as the log row - a status of Despatched with no external proof is an exception.
Open the archived PDF and confirm it is the template version in force at the event date per the form inventory.
Capture the proof record and the archived document into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled document traces to an external delivery proof and an archived PDF of the correct template version.

testing.step: Test the durable-medium and language conditions on the sample
actions: For every non-paper delivery check the stored consent timestamp, the recorded evidence of regular internet access under Art. 23(5) and a valid e-mail address on file at the despatch date.
Fail any electronic delivery where consent was captured after despatch or where paper was the recorded preference.
Check the document language matches the member state of the commitment or a recorded customer agreement to another language.
Confirm any paper-copy request in the period was served free within 5 business days from the archive.
testing.done: every non-paper delivery has pre-dated consent and access evidence, correct language, and paper requests were served within 5 business days.

testing.step: Re-perform the bind-step block on a live test transaction
actions: In the test environment create a quote, suppress the pre-contract pack despatch and attempt to conclude the contract.
Confirm the system blocks conclusion and that the block cannot be cleared without a reason code and a manager-grade approver.
Repeat for an IBIP journey where the costs-and-charges disclosure is missing.
Screenshot the block and the override dialogue into the workpaper as evidence the control operates as designed.
testing.done: the conclusion block is demonstrated to operate for both standard and IBIP journeys, with the override path evidenced.

testing.step: Test the failed-delivery queue for real closure
actions: Pull all delivery exception cases closed in the month and select 20 by seeded random selection.
Confirm each closure carries a re-issue with a new proof reference or a traced-customer case, not a status change alone.
Compute the days from failure to re-issue and flag anything over 5 business days.
Check that the original notice-log row still shows the failure so the delay is not erased by the re-issue.
testing.done: every sampled closed exception shows a genuine re-issue or trace, an in-tolerance turnaround and an intact original failure record.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and detriment
actions: Raise an issue per exception with policy, host state, trigger event, days late and the IDD article engaged.
Assign a root cause (event feed delay, template version drift, vendor rejection, contact data quality, override misuse) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and, for packs despatched after conclusion, require the Consumer Affairs detriment assessment to be attached before the issue can close.
Carry open issues into the next month's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with root cause, owner, remediation date, attached detriment assessment where late, and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the timeliness rates for pre-contract packs, renewal invitations and IBIP statements against the 100% and 99% thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references and the customer-impact totals.
Have the independent reviewer, who did not operate the correspondence or renewal queues in the period, sign the workpaper.
Report to the conduct risk committee quarterly and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with stated conclusion, timeliness rates and a committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Accountable for the policy administration and correspondence configuration that hard-enforces IDD timing and content rules - document triggers, pre-conclusion despatch gate, IBIP suitability and sustainability-preference questioning, and template version control

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - the configuration backlog cites IDD (EU) 2016/97 Arts. 17(1), 20(1)-(5), 23 and 29(2) and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Arts. 9-11 and 16-18 as the control requirements, each restated as an acceptance criterion and re-verified with Compliance at every release

In-scope processes.value: Demand intake from Compliance -> configuration change -> test -> release for the EEA quote, bind, endorsement, renewal and IBIP anniversary journeys in the policy administration platform, correspondence engine, rules engine and portal front ends

In-scope systems.value: Policy administration configuration (product model, journey rules, document triggers), the correspondence engine template bindings, the customer and broker portals, and the batch scheduler running anniversary and renewal jobs

Compliance procedure documented.value: IDD System Control Configuration Standard - the enumerated list of enforced rules (no conclusion without despatched pre-contract pack, no IBIP bind without completed suitability and sustainability-preference capture, template version selected by event date, mandatory-field enforcement on demands-and-needs) with the config object that implements each

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance as requirement owner and the Head of IT as build owner; the control list is re-confirmed at each major release and at least annually

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per change - every configuration change touching an IDD-enforced rule must pass Compliance acceptance before the release gate, and no EEA-affecting release may deploy without a signed regression result on the IDD control set

Deadline reminders configured.value: Release calendar gate tasks at code freeze minus 10 working days for Compliance acceptance, plus automated alerts when a change request touches a config object tagged IDD-CONTROL

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Requirement-to-config traceability matrix, test scripts and results, release approvals and configuration baselines retained 10 years so the control state on any past date can be reconstructed

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any IDD control disabled, bypassed by a hotfix, or found failing in production is raised as a P2 incident with a compliance impact assessment and a back-out or fix deadline

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every change to an IDD-enforced rule, every emergency bypass and the closure of every IDD control incident

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All configuration changes released to EEA journeys in the period from the release log, plus the full IDD control set as it stands in the production configuration baseline at test date

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every enumerated IDD control must be present and enforcing in production - one disabled or bypassable control is a fail; any change released to an IDD control object without Compliance acceptance is a separate fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per change; regression of the full IDD control set runs at every release and is independently re-performed quarterly against the production configuration baseline

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have built, tested or approved the sampled configuration changes

Evidence location for test results.value: IDD configuration control workpaper (traceability matrix, release log extract, regression evidence, production re-performance screenshots) in the compliance evidence repository, linked from the change records

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Control list mapped to IDD articles, the configuration baseline showing each control enforcing, and dated test evidence, producible for a host-NCA systems-and-controls review within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Head of IT provides system evidence through Distribution Compliance, which owns the NCA dialogue; Regulatory Counsel clears any statement about a control that was not enforcing during a stated period

checklist.step: Take Compliance requirements in as testable configuration rules
actions: Open a requirement ticket per IDD rule with the article cited in the description - Art. 20(5) pre-conclusion despatch, Art. 20(1) demands and needs captured, Art. 23 durable-medium consent, Art. 29(2) annual IBIP statement, Delegated Regulation 2017/2359 Art. 9 suitability and sustainability preferences.
Write each as a Given/When/Then acceptance criterion naming the journey, the trigger and the expected system behaviour including the blocking behaviour.
Ask the Compliance Manager to accept the wording before build starts and record the acceptance on the ticket.
Label every such ticket IDD-CONTROL so the release gate can find them.
checklist.done: each IDD rule has a labelled ticket with a cited article, Given/When/Then criteria and recorded Compliance acceptance.

checklist.step: Map every rule to the configuration object that will enforce it
actions: For each ticket name the implementing object: validation rule set on the bind step, document trigger on the quote and issue events, product model field with required flag, batch job definition for the anniversary run.
Record the object name, its environment path and its current version in the traceability matrix.
Prefer a platform validation rule over a UI-only check so broker portal and API-bound business is covered by the same enforcement.
Flag any rule that can only be enforced downstream and escalate it to the Compliance Manager as a residual risk before building it.
checklist.done: the traceability matrix links every IDD rule to a named, versioned configuration object and any UI-only enforcement is escalated.

checklist.step: Build the pre-conclusion despatch gate
actions: Add a bind-step validation that reads the notice log for a Despatched pre-contract pack against the quote and blocks issue where it is absent or failed.
Apply the rule at the service layer so broker portal, API and batch-bound business all hit it, not only the internal desktop journey.
Build the override as a separate, permission-gated path requiring a reason code from a fixed list and a manager-grade approver id.
Emit an audit event on every block and every override carrying quote id, user, reason code and timestamp.
checklist.done: conclusion is blocked at the service layer without a despatched pack, and overrides require a coded reason, a manager approver and emit an audit event.

checklist.step: Build the demands-and-needs and suitability capture enforcement
actions: Make the demands-and-needs question set mandatory on the quote screen with typed fields, not free text, so the answers can be reported and tested.
For IBIPs add the Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Art. 9 suitability block including knowledge and experience, financial situation, ability to bear losses, risk tolerance and objectives.

Add the sustainability-preferences questions required since 2 August 2022 by Regulation (EU) 2021/1257, with the Taxonomy-aligned, SFDR sustainable-investment and principal-adverse-impact options as discrete captured values.
Block bind where the suitability assessment result is Unsuitable unless a documented customer-instructed non-advised route is selected, and record which route was taken.
checklist.done: demands-and-needs and IBIP suitability including sustainability preferences are captured as typed mandatory data and an unsuitable result blocks bind.

checklist.step: Bind documents to events with date-effective template selection
actions: Configure each document trigger from the approved trigger-to-document map: quote issue, bind, endorsement, renewal invitation, IBIP anniversary, cancellation.
Set template resolution to select the version effective on the transaction date for that product, host state, language and channel, so back-dated transactions render the historic pack.
Load the host-state renewal lead times onto the product record as data so a change of law is a data update, not a code release.
Fail the job loudly on an unresolved template rather than rendering a default document.
checklist.done: every trigger resolves a date-effective, state-specific template and an unresolved template fails the job instead of substituting a default.

checklist.step: Schedule the timing-driven batch jobs
actions: Schedule the renewal invitation job to run daily selecting policies at renewal date minus the host-state lead time plus a print lead-time buffer.
Schedule the IBIP anniversary job at anniversary minus 10 working days so the Art. 29(2) statement can be despatched within 30 days of the anniversary.
Configure job failure alerting to page the on-call operator and to hold the run for restart rather than skipping the day's population.
Prove the calendar handles host-state public holidays and month-end boundaries with a dry run over a full year of dates.
checklist.done: renewal and anniversary jobs run on host-state-aware calendars, failures hold for restart, and a full-year dry run passes.

checklist.step: Wire the audit trail and the reportable control data
actions: Stream the notice-log, block, override and suitability-result events into the warehouse with policy, quote, user, timestamp, host state and channel.
Build the conformed model behind the delivery dashboard so operations and audit read the same figures.
Set field-level data quality checks for null despatch timestamps, null host state and unresolved template ids, alerting the Data Quality Analyst on breach.
Retain the event history for 10 years so the control state on any past date can be reconstructed.
checklist.done: control events land in the warehouse with quality checks, feed one conformed reporting model and are retained for 10 years.

checklist.step: Write the regression suite for the IDD control set
actions: Automate one test per acceptance criterion, including the negative cases - attempt to bind without a pack, without demands and needs, with an unsuitable IBIP result, with a missing sustainability answer.
Add channel coverage: desktop, broker portal, customer portal and API bind, since each can bypass a UI-only rule.
Add a date-effective template test that back-dates a transaction and asserts the historic template renders.
Wire the suite into the release pipeline as a mandatory gate that fails the build on any IDD-CONTROL test failure.
checklist.done: an automated IDD control suite covering positive, negative, multi-channel and date-effective cases gates the release pipeline.

checklist.step: Test the configuration in a production-like environment
actions: Execute the suite in the pre-production environment refreshed with masked production data covering every EEA host state written.
Run the manual exploratory cases the automation cannot cover - printed pack layout, portal notification wording, ombudsman address by state.
Log every defect against the originating requirement ticket so traceability survives to the release record.
Re-run the full suite after the last defect fix rather than retesting only the fixed case.
checklist.done: the full suite passes in a production-like environment on the final build with every defect closed against its requirement.

checklist.step: Get Compliance acceptance before the release gate
actions: Review the requirement-to-test evidence pack at code freeze minus 10 working days.
Re-read the acceptance criteria against the current article text and confirm no article has changed since the ticket was written.
Record acceptance or rejection on each IDD-CONTROL ticket with name and date; rejection holds the change, not the release of the rest.
Refuse acceptance where evidence is a screenshot of a passing test in a non-production-like environment.
checklist.done: every IDD-CONTROL ticket carries a dated Compliance acceptance or a hold, based on production-like evidence.

checklist.step: Release under change control with a back-out plan
actions: Raise the change record listing every IDD-CONTROL object touched, the Compliance acceptance references and the regression result.
Attach the back-out plan and the specific verification steps to run in production immediately after deployment.
Obtain CAB approval with the Compliance Manager recorded as an approver for IDD-affecting changes.
Deploy in the approved window and capture the deployment log and configuration version in the change record.
checklist.done: the change record holds the object list, Compliance approval, regression result, back-out plan and post-deploy verification steps.

checklist.step: Verify the controls in production straight after deployment
actions: Run the post-deploy verification script in production: create a controlled test quote per affected host state and confirm the pack renders and the bind block fires.
Confirm the batch jobs are scheduled and enabled with the correct host-state calendars.
Confirm the audit events are landing in the warehouse for the test transactions.
Cancel the test quotes and record the verification result on the change record within the deployment window.
checklist.done: post-deploy verification in production confirms rendering, blocking, scheduling and audit capture, recorded on the change record.

checklist.step: Control emergency changes so a fix cannot silently disable a rule
actions: Require every emergency change to declare whether it touches an IDD-CONTROL object and to name the Compliance approver reached at the time.
Where a control is temporarily disabled, open a P2 incident on the spot with the affected journeys, host states and expected duration.
Restore the control and re-run its regression tests before the incident can be closed.
Report every emergency IDD change to the Compliance Manager within one business day with the exposure window.
checklist.done: no emergency change touches an IDD control without a named Compliance approver, an incident record and a post-restore regression.

checklist.step: Baseline and monitor the production configuration
actions: Snapshot the production configuration of every IDD-CONTROL object weekly with its version and enabled/disabled state.
Diff each snapshot against the approved baseline and alert the Head of IT and the Compliance Manager on any unapproved difference.
Investigate every difference to a change record; a difference with no change record is treated as an unauthorised change.
Publish the weekly diff result to the IT compliance dashboard.
checklist.done: a weekly configuration diff against the approved baseline runs, and every difference is tied to a change record or raised as unauthorised.

checklist.step: File the configuration evidence set
actions: File the traceability matrix, test evidence, Compliance acceptances, change records and configuration baselines under the release.
Apply a 10-year retention label so a past control state can be evidenced to a regulator.
Confirm the record is searchable by IDD article, configuration object and release date.
Hand the release summary to the Controls Analyst for the quarterly independent re-performance.
checklist.done: a retention-labelled, article-searchable configuration evidence set is filed and handed to the independent reviewer.

testing.step: Build the population of IDD-affecting configuration changes
actions: Extract every change record deployed to EEA journeys in the quarter with its touched-object list from the release log.
Add every change touching an object on the IDD-CONTROL traceability matrix, whether or not it carried the label, by joining on object name.
Reconcile the change count to the deployment log from the pipeline so an undocumented deployment cannot hide.
testing.done: the change population reconciles to the deployment log and includes every change touching an IDD control object.

testing.step: Reconcile the control list to the production configuration baseline
actions: Take the current production configuration snapshot and match every IDD rule on the traceability matrix to a live, enabled object.
List any rule with no implementing object, any object disabled, and any object whose version is not the approved one.
Treat a rule enforced only in the desktop UI while broker portal and API journeys bypass it as a control gap, not a documentation issue.
testing.done: every IDD rule maps to a live, enabled, approved-version production object or is listed as a control gap.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of changes and controls
actions: Take 100% of emergency changes and 100% of changes that disabled or bypassed an IDD control.
Take 15 standard changes by seeded random selection plus the full enumerated IDD control set for re-performance.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all emergency and bypass changes, and includes the full control set.

testing.step: Re-perform the blocking controls in the live system
actions: In a controlled production or production-mirror session, attempt to bind a quote with no despatched pre-contract pack and record the system response.
Repeat through the broker portal and through the bind API with the same suppressed condition to prove service-layer enforcement.
Attempt an IBIP bind with the suitability assessment incomplete and with the sustainability-preference question unanswered.
Screenshot each block, or each successful bypass, into the workpaper - a bypass is an exception regardless of how rarely the path is used.
testing.done: each blocking control is independently re-performed across desktop, portal and API with the outcome captured.

testing.step: Re-perform date-effective template resolution
actions: Create a back-dated transaction whose effective date falls before the current template's effective-from date and render the pack.
Compare the rendered template version to the form inventory row in force at that date.
Repeat for two host states with different language variants to prove state and language resolution.
Fail any case rendering the current template for a historic date or falling back to a default document.
testing.done: date-effective, state-specific and language-specific template resolution is demonstrated with rendered evidence.

testing.step: Trace sampled changes to acceptance, testing and approval
actions: For each sampled change open the requirement ticket and confirm a dated Compliance acceptance pre-dating the release.
Open the pipeline run and confirm the IDD control regression suite executed and passed on the deployed build, not an earlier one.
Confirm the change record names the touched IDD objects, the back-out plan and the post-deploy verification result.
Flag any change deployed with the regression gate skipped or overridden.
testing.done: every sampled change traces to pre-dated Compliance acceptance, a passing regression on the deployed build and a completed post-deploy verification.

testing.step: Test the batch job scheduling and the date maths
actions: Pull the scheduler definitions for the renewal invitation and IBIP anniversary jobs and read the offsets configured.
Recompute the renewal selection date as renewal date minus host-state lead time minus print buffer for three states and compare to the job output for a sampled run day.
Recompute the IBIP selection date as anniversary minus 10 working days across a public holiday and confirm the calendar handled it.
Check the job run history for failed or skipped days and confirm each was restarted with the full population.
testing.done: job offsets are independently recomputed and the run history shows no population skipped on a failed day.

testing.step: Test the audit event completeness against transactions
actions: Count bind transactions in the source system for a sample week and compare to the count of bind audit events in the warehouse.
Check every override event carries a reason code, an approver id and a timestamp, and reconcile the override count to the weekly override report sent to Compliance.
Run the null checks on despatch timestamp, host state and template id and quantify the failure rate.
Fail the test where the reporting model and the source system disagree by more than 0.1%.
testing.done: warehouse control events reconcile to source transactions within tolerance and every override carries a complete attribute set.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and exposure window
actions: Raise an issue per control gap or bypassed change with the object, the journeys and host states affected, and the dates the control was not enforcing.
Estimate the transactions concluded in the exposure window and hand the list to Consumer Affairs for a detriment assessment.
Assign a root cause (rule built in UI only, regression gate skipped, unapproved configuration change, calendar defect) and a named owner with a fix date.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with exposure window, affected transaction count, root cause, owner and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compare the count of enforcing controls to the enumerated IDD control set and state the shortfall.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the re-performance evidence and any exposure windows.
Have the independent reviewer, who built, tested or approved none of the sampled changes, sign the workpaper.
Report to the technology risk committee and the conduct risk committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, control shortfall count and dual committee reporting is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the Art. 10 knowledge-and-ability programme for everyone carrying out distribution - employees, tied agents, appointed representatives and the managers responsible for them - including the 15-hours-per-year continuing professional training requirement

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - IDD (EU) 2016/97 Art. 10(1)-(2) and Annex I minimum professional knowledge areas, Art. 10(2) second sub-paragraph 15 hours of continuing professional training or development per year, and Art. 10(3) good repute requirements, cross-read to each host state's transposed hours and evidencing rules

In-scope processes.value: Onboarding of any person carrying out distribution -> initial competence assessment -> annual CPD curriculum -> hours tracking -> annual attestation, covering non-life, life, IBIP and claims-facing distribution staff plus the managers responsible for them

In-scope systems.value: Learning management system holding the IDD curriculum, enrolments, completion records and CPD hours, fed from the HRIS population and reconciled to the producer register

Compliance procedure documented.value: IDD Knowledge and Ability Procedure - population definition, Annex I curriculum mapping by role, the 15-hour CPD rule, assessment pass mark, failure and re-test path, and the consequence of non-completion (removal from distribution activity)

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Chief HR Officer; reviewed annually before the training-year plan is published and on any host-state change to CPD hours

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual - the 15 CPD hours must be completed inside the training year ending 31 December; new joiners must pass the initial competence assessment before their first distribution activity; the annual attestation closes by 31 January

Deadline reminders configured.value: LMS reminders at 90, 60, 30 and 7 days before 31 December for anyone below 15 hours, manager escalation at 30 days, and a joiner reminder at day 5 and day 20 of employment against the pre-activity deadline

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Per-person training record - curriculum version, module completions, hours, assessment scores, attestation and manager sign-off - retained for the period of distribution activity plus 5 years

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Anyone distributing without a current competence record or below 15 CPD hours at year end is logged with the dates of unqualified activity, the business written in that window and the remediation decision

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every non-completion disposition, every removal from distribution activity and any decision to leave business written by an unqualified person in force

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every person who carried out distribution in the training year, built from the HRIS distribution-role population plus the tied-agent and appointed-representative register, joined to LMS records

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of the population must hold a passed initial assessment before first activity and 15 or more CPD hours at 31 December; any person distributing without a current record is a fail and triggers a business-written review

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual with continuous onboarding; completion is monitored monthly and the full independent test runs annually in January against the closed training year

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Compliance and Learning and Development and must not have delivered or administered the tested curriculum

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual IDD competence test workpaper (population reconciliation, hours recomputation, sampled certificates and assessment records, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-person competence register showing Annex I area coverage, hours, assessment results and attestation date, producible for a host-NCA or EIOPA request within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Distribution Compliance answers NCA competence queries through the home-state supervisor; HR provides employment records and Regulatory Counsel clears any admission of unqualified distribution activity

checklist.step: Define who counts as carrying out distribution
actions: Extract from the HRIS every job code that advises on, proposes, concludes or assists in the administration and performance of insurance contracts, including contact centre agents, underwriters who quote direct, and claims staff who administer contracts.
Add the managers responsible for distribution activity, who fall in scope under Art. 10(2), and the directors named in the Art. 10(3) good-repute requirement.
Add tied agents, appointed representatives and outsourced contact centre staff from the producer register - the obligation follows the activity, not the payroll.
Have the Head of Distribution confirm no distributing population is missing and record the confirmation date.
checklist.done: a confirmed in-scope population exists covering employees, managers, tied agents and outsourced distributing staff, with the confirming manager named.

checklist.step: Map the Annex I knowledge areas onto each role
actions: List the Annex I areas: terms and conditions of policies offered including ancillary risks; applicable laws governing distribution; claims handling; complaints handling; assessing customer needs; the insurance market; business ethics standards; and financial competence.

For life and IBIP roles add the Annex I(II) and (III) areas - policy terms and guarantees, the structure and risks of the products offered, tax and social regime, financial markets, financial and actuarial basics.
Build a role-to-area matrix showing which areas each job code must cover and the minimum depth.
Get the matrix approved by the Head of Compliance before the curriculum is built.
checklist.done: an approved role-to-Annex-I matrix names the required knowledge areas and depth for every in-scope job code.

checklist.step: Build the curriculum against the mapped areas
actions: Design one module per Annex I area with a stated learning objective, the credited hours and the assessment method.
Use the firm's own IPID, demands-and-needs statement and complaints route as the worked examples so the training matches the actual documents and systems.

Add the conduct modules Art. 17(1) demands - acting honestly, fairly and professionally in the best interests of customers, conflicts of interest and remuneration transparency, and cross-selling under Art. 24.
Tag every module with the Annex I area and the credited hours so completion reports can be read against the Directive.
Version the curriculum with an effective date so a person's record shows which version they took.
checklist.done: each Annex I area has a versioned module with an objective, credited hours, an assessment and firm-specific worked examples.

checklist.step: Set the assessment standard and the failure path
actions: Set the pass mark per assessment, randomise the question pool and prevent unlimited immediate retakes.
Write the failure path: a second attempt after mandatory re-study, a third failure escalating to the line manager and removal from distribution activity pending competence.
Include scenario questions requiring the learner to produce a personalised recommendation explaining why a product meets stated demands and needs, not only recall questions.
Have the Compliance Manager review and approve the question pool annually for currency against the Directive and the firm's products.
checklist.done: a Compliance-approved question pool, pass mark and documented failure path with a removal step exist and are live in the LMS.

checklist.step: Load the population and assign the curriculum
actions: Feed the in-scope population into the LMS from the HRIS nightly, driven by job code so a role change reassigns the curriculum automatically.
Assign the role-appropriate curriculum with a due date of 31 December for existing staff.
Load tied agents and outsourced staff through the external-learner route with the same curriculum and due dates.
Reconcile the LMS enrolment count to the HRIS and producer-register counts weekly and clear every difference.
checklist.done: every in-scope person, internal or external, holds an assigned curriculum and LMS enrolments reconcile weekly to HRIS and the producer register.

checklist.step: Gate new joiners before their first distribution activity
actions: Assign the initial competence curriculum on the day the offer is accepted, with completion required before the first customer contact.
Ask the Access Management Analyst to withhold quote and bind entitlement in the policy administration platform until the LMS records a pass.
Run the Art. 10(3) good-repute checks - criminal record certificate where the host state requires it, bankruptcy check and prior regulatory-register check - before activity starts.
Record the pass date, the entitlement grant date and the good-repute check outcomes on the personnel file.
checklist.done: no joiner holds quote or bind entitlement before a recorded assessment pass and completed good-repute checks.

checklist.step: Track the 15 CPD hours across the training year
actions: Credit hours only against modules with a stated learning objective and an assessment or verified attendance, per Art. 10(2).
Accept external hours - professional body courses, insurer product training, conferences - only with a certificate showing the provider, date, content and hours, uploaded to the record.
Show each person a running hours total in the LMS against the 15-hour requirement with the shortfall stated.
Reject unverifiable self-declared hours rather than crediting them provisionally.
checklist.done: every credited hour ties to an assessed module or an uploaded external certificate, and each person sees a running total against 15 hours.

checklist.step: Publish monthly completion and escalate the laggards
actions: Publish a monthly dashboard of hours completed by person, team, entity and host state, with the count below 15 hours and days remaining in the training year.
Send line managers their team's shortfall list and require a written completion plan for anyone below pace at 30 September.
Escalate anyone below 15 hours at 30 November to the Head of Distribution and the Compliance Manager.
Track the escalation to closure rather than re-reporting the same names each month.
checklist.done: a monthly hours dashboard exists, managers hold written plans for laggards, and November escalations are tracked to closure.

checklist.step: Deliver targeted training where conduct data says it is needed
actions: Take the quarter's complaint root causes, suitability file-review failures and mystery-shopping findings from the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
Build a short targeted module against the top themes - for example weak demands-and-needs capture or unclear remuneration disclosure - and assign it to the affected teams.
Deliver it inside 30 days of the finding and credit the hours to the CPD total.
Re-measure the theme in the next quarter's file review and report whether the training moved it.
checklist.done: each quarter's conduct findings produce a targeted module delivered within 30 days and a re-measured outcome the following quarter.

checklist.step: Run the annual attestation
actions: Issue the attestation in the first week of January to everyone in the training-year population.
Require each person to confirm the Annex I areas completed, the hours achieved and that they have not distributed products outside their competence.
Require the line manager to counter-attest that their team members are competent for the products they distribute.
Close attestation by 31 January and list every non-responder for escalation.
checklist.done: attestations and manager counter-attestations are closed by 31 January with a named non-responder list.

checklist.step: Remove uncompleted staff from distribution activity
actions: Take the 31 December shortfall list and the non-attestation list from Compliance.
Revoke quote, bind and advice entitlement in the policy administration platform and the broker portal for each named person, with the revocation timestamped.
Re-instate entitlement only on a recorded LMS completion and a Compliance Manager release.
Report the revocation and re-instatement list to the Head of Compliance monthly until the list is empty.
checklist.done: every non-completer has timestamped entitlement revocation and re-instatement only follows a recorded completion and Compliance release.

checklist.step: Maintain the tied-agent and outsourced-staff evidence
actions: Require each tied agent and outsourced contact centre to submit an annual competence return listing every distributing person, hours and assessment results.
Check the return against the firm's own registered-agent list and challenge any person distributing but not listed.
Include the Art. 10 obligation and the right to inspect records in the distribution agreement, and exercise inspection on at least two partners a year.
Suspend new business submission rights for a partner that fails to return or fails inspection.
checklist.done: every partner has a reconciled annual competence return, two partners are inspected, and failures lead to suspended submission rights.

checklist.step: Report competence to the governance body
actions: Present the annual competence position to the conduct risk committee: population, completion rate, shortfalls, removals and partner failures.
Report business written by anyone found unqualified, with the customer-impact assessment.
Record committee decisions on curriculum investment and on partner suspensions in the minutes.
Carry unresolved shortfalls into the next training year as opening items.
checklist.done: the committee minute records the completion position, unqualified-activity impact and decisions, with unresolved items carried forward.

checklist.step: Refresh the curriculum for the coming training year
actions: Re-read Annex I and the host-state transposition for any change to required areas or hours before publishing the new year's plan.
Update modules for product changes, new IPIDs, the sustainability-preferences questioning and any new EIOPA guidance.
Retire modules that no longer reflect the firm's products so learners cannot complete hours on withdrawn products.
Publish the new curriculum version with its effective date by 31 January.
checklist.done: a new curriculum version reflecting current Annex I, host-state rules and live products is published with an effective date by 31 January.

checklist.step: File the competence evidence set
actions: Export the per-person competence register with Annex I area coverage, hours, assessment scores and attestation dates for the closed training year.
File it with the curriculum version, the question pool approval and the partner returns under the training year.
Apply the activity-plus-5-years retention label so leavers' records survive.
