Confirm the register can be filtered by entity, host state, job code and product type for a regulator request.
checklist.done: a filterable, retention-labelled competence register for the closed training year is filed with curriculum and partner evidence.

testing.step: Build the population of people who carried out distribution
actions: Extract all employees holding an in-scope distribution job code at any point in the training year, including leavers and role changers, from the HRIS.
Add tied agents, appointed representatives and outsourced contact centre staff from the producer register and the partner returns.
Cross-check against the policy administration platform user list of everyone who actually issued a quote or bound a policy in the year - activity is the test, not the job title.
Reconcile the three sources and resolve every person present in activity but absent from the HRIS or partner list before sampling.
testing.done: the population reconciles HRIS, the producer register and actual system activity, and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to LMS enrolment and completion
actions: Join the population to the LMS on employee or partner id and list everyone with no enrolment and everyone with no completion record.
Compare each person's assigned curriculum to the approved role-to-Annex-I matrix and list any role assigned the wrong curriculum.
Treat anyone who bound business with no completion record as an automatic exception with no sampling judgement applied.
testing.done: every distributing person maps to a correctly assigned curriculum and a completion record, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Recompute the 15-hour CPD position independently
actions: Export raw completion records with credited hours and recompute each person's training-year total from the transaction rows rather than the LMS summary field.
Exclude hours credited to modules with no assessment or verified attendance and hours dated outside the training year, then recompute.
Compare the recomputed totals to the reported completion rate and quantify the difference.
List everyone below 15 hours on the recomputed basis, including anyone the LMS reported as compliant.
testing.done: hours are recomputed from raw records on a valid-credit basis and every recomputed shortfall is listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample across roles, entities and partners
actions: Take 100% of people below 15 recomputed hours, 100% of new joiners who bound business in their first 60 days, and 100% of IBIP-advising staff.
Take 25 further people by seeded random selection across host states, entities and partner organisations.
Record the seed, the population size, the strata and the selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers shortfalls, new joiners and IBIP advisers, and its method is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the Annex I coverage check on each sampled record
actions: Open the current Annex I text and list the required areas for the sampled person's role independently of the firm's matrix.
Open the person's completed modules and check each required area is genuinely covered, reading the module objective rather than trusting the tag.
For life and IBIP staff check the Annex I(II)/(III) areas including product structure, guarantees, tax regime and financial market basics.
Record a fail where an area is tagged but the module content does not cover it.
testing.done: each sampled record carries an independent Annex I coverage conclusion based on module content, not tags.

testing.step: Test the assessment records and the failure path
actions: Pull each sampled person's assessment attempts with dates, scores and the pass mark applied.
Confirm passes meet the approved pass mark and that no unlimited same-day retake pattern produced the pass.
For every third failure in the year check the record shows escalation to the line manager and removal from distribution activity.
Confirm the question pool version used was the Compliance-approved one for that date.
testing.done: sampled assessment records show valid passes on the approved pool and every third failure shows escalation and removal.

testing.step: Test the joiner gate against real activity dates
actions: For each sampled joiner compare the LMS pass date and the entitlement grant date to the timestamp of their first quote or bind.
Flag any first activity that pre-dates the pass or the entitlement grant and quantify the policies bound in that window.
Confirm the Art. 10(3) good-repute checks were completed and dated before the first activity.
Capture the system records for each flagged case into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled joiner's first activity post-dates their pass, entitlement and good-repute checks, or the exposure is quantified.

testing.step: Test external hours and partner competence returns
actions: For 15 externally credited hours open the uploaded certificate and confirm provider, date, content and hours match the credit given.
Reject and list any credit supported only by a self-declaration or a calendar invitation.
For three partner returns reconcile the listed people to the firm's registered-agent list and to submitted new business in the year.
Request the underlying training records from one partner and re-perform its hours calculation.
testing.done: external credits trace to valid certificates and at least one partner return is re-performed against underlying records.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and business impact
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the person, role, entity, the shortfall or gap, and the policies they bound while unqualified.
Assign a root cause (population feed missed the role, wrong curriculum assigned, unverified external hours, partner return unreconciled) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and require a customer-impact review with Consumer Affairs where business was bound by an unqualified person.
Carry every open issue into the next training year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with root cause, owner, bound-business impact, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the recomputed completion rate against the 100% threshold and state the number of people who distributed while unqualified.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references and the business-impact totals.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither delivered nor administered the curriculum, sign the workpaper.
Report to the audit committee and the conduct risk committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, recomputed completion rate and dual committee reporting is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Heads the complaints management function required by the EIOPA complaints-handling guidelines, owning registration, handling within host-state deadlines, thematic root-cause analysis of IDD-related complaints and reporting to the conduct risk committee

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - IDD (EU) 2016/97 Art. 14 (complaints procedures), Art. 15 (out-of-court redress) and Art. 17(1), read with the EIOPA Guidelines on Complaints-Handling by Insurance Undertakings (EIOPA-BoS-12/069) and by Insurance Intermediaries (EIOPA-BoS-13/164), plus each host state's transposed acknowledgement and final-response deadlines

In-scope processes.value: Complaint capture across contact centre, portal, e-mail, broker and ombudsman routes -> registration and classification against IDD cause codes -> investigation and final response -> thematic root-cause analysis -> remediation and product/process change, for every EEA host state written

In-scope systems.value: Complaints case management holding the register, cause codes, deadlines and correspondence, fed from the contact centre platform and the portal and reported through the analytics layer

Compliance procedure documented.value: IDD Complaints Handling and Root Cause Procedure - what counts as a complaint (any expression of dissatisfaction about the provision of, or failure to provide, an insurance service), the IDD cause taxonomy, host-state deadlines, redress authority levels, ombudsman referral wording and the quarterly thematic analysis method

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the conduct risk committee; reviewed annually and on any host-state or EIOPA guideline change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Continuous - acknowledgement within 5 business days of receipt, holding updates every 20 business days, final response within the host-state limit (40 business days in Ireland, 3 months as the outer EU norm), ombudsman referral rights stated in the final response, and NCA complaints returns on the host-state reporting calendar

Deadline reminders configured.value: Case-level SLA clocks with alerts at day 3 for unacknowledged cases, day 15 and day 30 for open cases, and daily breach reporting to the Complaints Manager and the owning team leader

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Complaint file - original expression of dissatisfaction, investigation notes, evidence considered, final response letter, redress calculation and ombudsman correspondence - retained for the life of the contract plus 10 years

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Breached deadlines, mis-registered complaints treated as service requests and repeat root causes without a closed remediation action are logged as conduct exceptions with owner and due date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off each quarter's root-cause conclusions, the remediation actions raised and the decision on proactive redress to non-complaining customers affected by the same cause

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All complaints registered in the quarter with an IDD-related cause code, plus a reverse-population sweep of contact-centre and portal contacts classified as service requests to catch unregistered complaints

Pass/fail thresholds.value: At least 98% acknowledged within 5 business days and 98% final-responded inside the host-state limit; zero tolerance on a complaint closed without a stated ombudsman referral right; every root cause appearing in two consecutive quarters must have an owned remediation action or the test fails

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; SLA monitoring is daily, quality file reviews are monthly, and the independent thematic root-cause test runs quarterly on the closed-complaint population

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have handled, approved or signed the final response on any sampled complaint

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly complaints root-cause workpaper (register extract, SLA recomputation, sampled file reviews, reverse-population sweep, theme analysis, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Complaints register export by host state and cause code with SLA outcomes, the quarterly thematic report and the remediation action log, producible for a host-NCA or ombudsman thematic request within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Consumer Affairs owns individual ombudsman and NCA case responses; the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager owns thematic findings and escalates systemic conduct issues to the home-state supervisor with Regulatory Counsel clearance

checklist.step: Define what must be registered as a complaint
actions: Adopt the EIOPA definition - any expression of dissatisfaction addressed to the firm about the provision of, or failure to provide, an insurance service - and write it into the procedure with worked examples.
List the channels that must register: contact centre calls, e-mail, portal messages, social media, letters, broker referrals and ombudsman first contacts.
State expressly that dissatisfaction resolved on the first call is still a complaint for registration and root-cause purposes, even where no redress follows.
Brief the Contact Center Ops Manager and require the definition to be posted in the agent knowledge base.
checklist.done: the registration definition, channel list and first-call-resolution rule are documented and published to agents.

checklist.step: Build the IDD cause taxonomy into the case tool
actions: Create cause codes mapped to IDD obligations: pre-contract information not received or late (Art. 20(5)), IPID content unclear (Art. 20(4)), remuneration or status not disclosed (Arts. 18-19), advice did not match demands and needs (Art. 20(1)), unsuitable IBIP recommendation (Delegated Regulation 2017/2359 Art. 9), cross-selling not explained (Art. 24), pressure selling or best-interests failure (Art. 17(1)).
Add product, host state, distribution channel and selling entity or agent as mandatory case attributes so themes can be cut by source.
Make the cause code mandatory at closure and prevent a generic Other code without free-text justification reviewed monthly.
Publish the code definitions in the agent knowledge base with an example complaint per code.
checklist.done: IDD-mapped cause codes with mandatory product, state, channel and agent attributes are live and defined for handlers.

checklist.step: Register and acknowledge every complaint inside five business days
actions: Open a case on receipt recording the date and channel of receipt, the customer's own words, the policy and the host state.
Send the written acknowledgement within 5 business days naming the handler, the process, the expected timescale and the customer's right to go to the out-of-court redress body under Art. 15.
Start the host-state SLA clock from the receipt date, not the registration date, so a late registration does not buy time.
Where the complaint concerns a tied agent or broker, notify that partner in writing and request their file the same day.
checklist.done: each complaint has a case with the customer's own words, an acknowledgement within 5 business days and an SLA clock running from receipt.

checklist.step: Investigate against the evidence the customer never sees
actions: Pull the archived pre-contract pack, the demands-and-needs statement and, for IBIPs, the suitability assessment as they were issued, from the document archive.
Pull the call recording and the notice-log despatch proof for the transaction in question.
Test the complaint against what was actually disclosed and when - was the IPID despatched before conclusion, did the recommendation explain why the product met the stated needs.
Record on the case which evidence was reviewed and what it showed, so a later reviewer or ombudsman can follow the reasoning.
checklist.done: each investigation records the archived pack, despatch proof, call evidence and the conclusion each supports.

checklist.step: Decide redress and apply it consistently
actions: Apply the authority matrix: handler level, team leader level and Complaints Manager level by redress value and by whether a conduct breach is admitted.
Where the pre-contract information failed, put the customer back in the position they would have been in - restart a cancellation period, honour the disclosed terms, or refund premium with interest.
Check whether the same defect affects other customers before settling on an individual basis, and flag it to the quarterly theme review.
Record the redress calculation and its basis on the case, not only the amount paid.
checklist.done: each upheld complaint carries an authorised redress decision with a recorded calculation basis and a check for wider impact.

checklist.step: Issue the final response with the redress and referral rights
actions: Issue the final response inside the host-state limit, stating the outcome, the reasons and the evidence relied on in plain language.
Name the out-of-court redress body for that host state with its address, website and any time limit for referral, as Art. 15 requires.
Where the response will be late, send a holding update every 20 business days explaining why and when a decision is expected.
Archive the final response against the policy and close the case with the cause code and outcome.
checklist.done: every final response is issued inside the host-state limit, names the correct redress body and is archived against the policy.

checklist.step: Sweep for complaints that were never registered
actions: Run a monthly keyword and speech-analytics sweep across contact records for dissatisfaction language - mis-sold, never told, not explained, want to cancel because.
Pull the flagged contacts that were closed as service requests and have a Senior Contact Center Agent review each against the registration definition.
Register retrospectively any that should have been complaints, with the original contact date as the receipt date for SLA purposes.
Feed the miss rate by team into agent coaching and report it monthly to the Complaints Manager.
checklist.done: a monthly sweep runs, missed complaints are retrospectively registered from the original contact date and the miss rate is reported by team.

checklist.step: Handle ombudsman and NCA referrals as a distinct queue
actions: Log every out-of-court body or NCA referral with the reference, the body, the receipt date and the response deadline set by that body.
Assemble the file from the archive - pre-contract pack, despatch proof, demands-and-needs statement, call recording, final response - rather than re-creating documents.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear any submission that concedes a breach of an IDD obligation before it is sent.
Record the body's decision and, where the firm is overturned, raise a root-cause action rather than treating it as a one-off.
checklist.done: every referral has a logged deadline, a file assembled from archived evidence, counsel clearance where a breach is conceded and a recorded outcome.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly thematic root-cause analysis
actions: Extract the quarter's closed complaints and rank cause codes by volume, by upheld rate and by redress paid, cut by product, host state, channel and selling agent.
Trend each theme over the last eight quarters so an emerging cause is separated from noise.
Overlay sales volume so a small line with a high complaints-per-1000-policies rate is not hidden by a large line's absolute numbers.
Identify the top five themes and the outlier agents or partners and hand the analysis to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: a quarterly analysis ranks and trends causes normalised to sales volume and names the top themes and outlier distributors.

checklist.step: Trace each theme to the process or product that caused it
actions: For each top theme read a set of the underlying complaint files rather than working from the code alone - codes drift, files do not.
Name the failing control: disclosure content, despatch timing, system configuration, training gap, incentive design or partner behaviour.
Where incentive design is implicated, review the remuneration arrangement against Art. 17(3) - no arrangement may conflict with the duty to act in the customer's best interests.
Write a one-page cause statement per theme naming the accountable owner for the fix.
checklist.done: each top theme has a file-based cause statement naming the failing control and an accountable owner.

checklist.step: Raise and drive the remediation actions
actions: Raise one action per cause statement with the owner, the specific change required and a due date inside the next quarter.

Route disclosure fixes to the Insurance Product Manager, configuration fixes to the Head of IT, training fixes to the Learning Development Manager and partner behaviour to the Producer Compliance Manager.
Require evidence of the change - a new template version, a released configuration, a delivered module - before an action can be closed.
Escalate any theme recurring for two consecutive quarters with an open action to the conduct risk committee.
checklist.done: every cause statement has an owned, dated action closed only on evidence of the change, with two-quarter recurrences escalated.

checklist.step: Decide on proactive redress beyond the complainants
actions: For each upheld systemic theme, size the affected population from the policy administration data using the same defect criteria.
Propose a redress approach - contact and offer, automatic payment, or restart of a cancellation period - with the estimated cost.
Take the proposal to the conduct risk committee with Regulatory Counsel's view on whether host-NCA notification is required.
Record the decision, including a decision not to redress, with the reasoning.
checklist.done: each systemic upheld theme has a sized affected population and a recorded committee decision on proactive redress.

checklist.step: Report complaints to governance and to the regulators
actions: Report to the conduct risk committee quarterly: volumes, SLA performance, upheld rate, redress paid, top themes, open actions and ombudsman overturns.
Prepare the host-state NCA complaints returns on their reporting calendar using the same register extract so internal and regulatory figures agree.
Reconcile the return to the register before submission and keep the reconciliation with the submitted file.
Report material adverse trends to the board risk committee without waiting for the quarterly cycle.
checklist.done: committee reporting and NCA returns are produced from one reconciled register extract, with material trends escalated immediately.

checklist.step: Run monthly quality file reviews on closed complaints
actions: Select 20 closed complaints a month across handlers, host states and cause codes.
Score each on registration accuracy, evidence gathered, fairness of the outcome, clarity of the final response and correct redress-body wording.
Feed individual scores to team leaders for coaching and aggregate themes to the Complaints Manager.
Re-open and re-respond to any file where the outcome was wrong, rather than noting it as a quality point.
checklist.done: 20 files a month are scored on five criteria, wrong outcomes are re-opened and themes reach the Complaints Manager.

checklist.step: File the quarterly complaints evidence pack
actions: Assemble the register extract, SLA performance, thematic analysis, cause statements, action log and committee minutes for the quarter.
File under the quarter with the contract-life-plus-10-years retention label.
Confirm the extract can be filtered by host state, cause code, product, channel and selling agent for a regulator request.
Hand the pack to the Consumer Affairs Manager as the independent reviewer for the quarterly test.
checklist.done: a filterable, retention-labelled quarterly complaints pack is filed and handed to the independent reviewer.

testing.step: Build the complaints population for the quarter
actions: Extract every complaint received in the quarter with receipt date, host state, product, channel, cause code, SLA dates and outcome.
Add complaints registered retrospectively from the contact-centre sweep, using the original contact date as receipt.
Reconcile the extract to the volumes reported to the conduct risk committee and to the host-state NCA returns and resolve every difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population reconciles to committee and regulatory reported volumes and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Run a reverse population sweep for unregistered complaints
actions: Independently query the contact platform for the quarter's contacts containing dissatisfaction language and closed as service requests, using your own keyword list rather than the operational one.
Sample 40 of the flagged contacts and read or listen to each against the EIOPA complaint definition.
Count those that should have been registered and extrapolate the under-registration rate to the population.
Compare the extrapolated rate to the operational sweep's reported miss rate and explain any difference.
testing.done: an independent under-registration rate is computed from a sampled sweep and compared to the operational miss rate.

testing.step: Recompute the SLA performance from raw dates
actions: Recompute acknowledgement days as acknowledgement date minus receipt date in business days on the host-state calendar, not the system's stored flag.
Recompute final-response days against each host state's limit re-derived from the transposition text rather than the field held on the case.
Count cases where the SLA clock was restarted or the receipt date amended after opening and treat each as a potential SLA manipulation to be examined.
Compare the recomputed percentages to the reported 98% thresholds and quantify the difference.
testing.done: acknowledgement and final-response timeliness are independently recomputed on host-state calendars and reconciled to reported figures.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of complaint files
actions: Take 100% of ombudsman overturns, 100% of complaints with redress above the Complaints Manager authority limit and 100% of IDD pre-contract-information cause codes.
Take 25 further files by seeded random selection stratified by host state, cause code and handler.
Record the seed, the population size, the strata and the selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers overturns, high-redress and IDD-information causes, and its method is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the cause classification on the sampled files
actions: Read the customer's own words on each sampled case and assign your own cause code against the taxonomy before looking at the recorded code.
Compare and list every mis-classification, particularly IDD disclosure failures coded as service or claims issues, which suppress the theme.
Recompute the top-five theme ranking on your own codes and compare it to the reported ranking.
Treat a changed theme ranking as a finding on the analysis, not only on the individual files.
testing.done: cause codes are independently re-assigned, mis-classifications listed, and the theme ranking recomputed and compared.

testing.step: Trace each sampled file to the underlying transaction evidence
actions: Pull the archived pre-contract pack and the notice-log despatch proof for each sampled complaint's policy.
Check the investigation actually considered them and that the conclusion drawn is supported by what they show.
Where the complaint alleged late or missing information, verify the despatch timestamp against the conclusion date independently.
Fail any file that upheld or rejected a complaint without opening the archived evidence.
testing.done: every sampled file's outcome is tested against the archived pack and despatch proof, with unsupported outcomes failed.

testing.step: Test the final response content and redress-body wording
actions: Read each sampled final response for a stated outcome, stated reasons and plain language a customer could act on.
Check the named out-of-court redress body is the correct one for the host state, with a current address and any referral time limit stated, per Art. 15.
Fail any closure with no referral rights stated regardless of the outcome - this is the zero-tolerance item.
Check holding updates were sent every 20 business days on any case that ran past the limit.
testing.done: every sampled final response states outcome, reasons and correct host-state referral rights, with holding updates evidenced on late cases.

testing.step: Recompute the redress and test consistency across like cases
actions: Recompute the redress on 10 upheld cases from the stated basis - premium refunded, interest applied, cancellation period restarted.
Compare redress across cases with the same cause code and similar facts and list unexplained differences by handler.
Check the authority matrix was respected - no handler-level approval on an amount above their limit.
Confirm the payment actually reached the customer by tracing to the payment record.
testing.done: redress is recomputed, consistency across like cases is tested, authority limits verified and payments traced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with the case reference, host state, cause code, the failure found and its customer impact.
Assign a root cause (registration definition not applied, cause code drift, SLA clock manipulation, missing redress-body wording, theme with no closed action) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and, where under-registration or a systemic theme is found, require the affected-population sizing to be attached before closure.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with root cause, owner, remediation date, population sizing where systemic, and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: State the recomputed acknowledgement and final-response rates against the 98% thresholds and the under-registration rate from the reverse sweep.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references and any theme recurring without a closed action.
Have the independent reviewer, who handled or approved none of the sampled complaints, sign the workpaper.
Report to the conduct risk committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, recomputed SLA and under-registration rates and a committee reporting date is filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual internal audit of IDD customer documentation - content against Arts. 18-20 and 29 and timing against Art. 20(5) and Art. 23 - delivered independently of Compliance and Policy Administration, with findings reported to the audit committee

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - the audit programme cites IDD (EU) 2016/97 Arts. 17-20, 23 and 29 and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1469 as the audit criteria, re-read from EUR-Lex at planning and confirmed against each in-scope host state's transposition before fieldwork

In-scope processes.value: Second-line disclosure build, notice generation and delivery, system configuration and complaints root cause, audited end to end across a risk-selected set of EEA host states, products and distribution channels

In-scope systems.value: Audit workpapers, sampling and issue tracking in the audit platform, drawing evidence from the policy administration platform, the document archive and the complaints case tool

Compliance procedure documented.value: IDD Documentation Audit Programme - risk assessment and scoping method, population build, sampling standard, the content test grid per IDD article, the timing recomputation method, issue rating scale and reporting route

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the audit committee in the annual audit plan; the detailed programme is approved by the Chief Audit Executive and refreshed before each engagement

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual - fieldwork completed and the draft report issued within 30 days of fieldwork close, management responses due within 15 business days, final report to the audit committee at its next scheduled meeting

Deadline reminders configured.value: Audit platform milestone alerts at planning sign-off, fieldwork close, draft issue, response due date, and monthly ageing alerts on overdue audit actions to each action owner and their executive

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Audit file - programme, population and sampling records, tested specimens, timing recomputations, exception schedules, management responses and the signed report - retained 10 years under the audit records policy

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every documentation defect is raised as a rated audit issue with the IDD article breached, affected policy count, agreed action, owner and due date, and is tracked to evidenced closure

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Closes each audit issue only on inspected evidence of the fix and reports any action closed without evidence to the audit committee

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All policies concluded in the audit period in the selected host states, joined to the notice log and the document archive, plus the full form inventory for the selected products

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on a missing mandatory disclosure element or a pack despatched after conclusion; content defect rate above 2% of the sample rates the issue High; any repeat of a prior-year finding is automatically rated High regardless of volume

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous, second-line testing is monthly and quarterly; internal audit tests annually on a full-year population with a follow-up review at six months on High-rated issues

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Every workpaper is reviewed by an audit team member who did not perform the test, and the report is reviewed by the Chief Audit Executive who holds no operational role

Evidence location for test results.value: IDD documentation audit file in the audit platform, with the signed report and the issue log cross-linked to the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Signed audit report, issue log with agreed actions and closure evidence, and the underlying sample schedules, producible to a host NCA or to EIOPA within 10 business days

checklist.step: Risk-assess and scope the engagement
actions: Rank EEA host states and products by new business volume, complaint density on IDD cause codes, recent product launches and prior-year findings.
Select the host states, products and channels for fieldwork and write the rationale into the planning memo, including what is deliberately out of scope.
Confirm the audit is independent - no auditor on the team has advised on the disclosure build or the configuration being tested.
Obtain audit committee endorsement of the scope in the annual plan and record the date.
checklist.done: a planning memo names the selected states, products and channels with a risk rationale, an independence confirmation and committee endorsement.

checklist.step: Build the audit criteria grid from the source texts
actions: Open the current EUR-Lex text of IDD Arts. 17-20, 23 and 29 and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1469 and write each testable requirement as a grid row.
Add a column per selected host state for transposed add-ons taken from the national text, not from the firm's own matrix.
State for each row what evidence would prove compliance and what would prove failure, before any evidence is seen.
Have the grid reviewed by the Audit Analyst and, for legal interpretation only, by Regulatory Counsel without letting counsel set the audit conclusion.
checklist.done: an independently sourced criteria grid exists with per-state add-ons and stated pass/fail evidence for every row.

checklist.step: Walk through the end-to-end process before testing
actions: Sit with the Insurance Product Manager, the Policy Admin Ops Lead and the Configuration Engineer and walk one product from disclosure build to customer despatch.
Record the actual control points, the systems touched and the hand-offs, and compare them to the documented procedure.
Note every point where a control depends on a person remembering rather than a system enforcing.
Confirm the walkthrough with the process owners in writing so the process description cannot be disputed at reporting.
checklist.done: a written, owner-confirmed walkthrough records the real control points and every manual dependency.

checklist.step: Build the audit population from the source systems
actions: Extract every policy concluded in the audit period in the selected host states with conclusion timestamp, product, channel, selling agent and language.
Join to the notice log on policy and event to attach generation and despatch timestamps and template versions.
Reconcile the policy count to the financial new-business production report and resolve every difference before sampling.
Have the extract query and its parameters reviewed by a second auditor and saved into the audit file so it can be re-run.
checklist.done: a reconciled, reviewer-checked and re-runnable population extract exists joining policies to their notice records.

checklist.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of IBIP sales, 100% of sales in host states entered during the period and 100% of packs despatched at or after conclusion.
Take 40 further policies by seeded random selection stratified across product, host state and channel.
Record the seed, population size, strata, sample size rationale and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn by a reviewer.
Lock the sample before fieldwork so it cannot be adjusted once results start arriving.
checklist.done: a locked, reproducible sample covering IBIPs, new states and late packs is documented with its selection rationale.

checklist.step: Test the content of each sampled pack against the criteria grid
actions: Open the archived pack for each sampled policy - the version the customer received, not the current template.

Score each grid row pass or fail: Art. 18 identity and register number, Art. 19 remuneration type and fair-and-personal-analysis statement, Art. 20(1) demands and needs, Art. 20(4) IPID presence, Art. 29 IBIP aggregate costs.
Check the IPID against Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1469 - title, status line, prescribed headings, icons and the two-sided-A4 print limit.
Record the page and paragraph reference for every pass and the precise absence for every fail, and attach the pack to the workpaper.
checklist.done: every sampled pack has a row-by-row scored grid with page references for passes and precise descriptions of failures.

checklist.step: Recompute the timing on every sampled policy
actions: Compute despatch timestamp minus conclusion timestamp for each pre-contract pack and list every non-negative result as a breach of Art. 20(5).
Compute the interval against the firm's own documented 'in good time' standard and list packs that met the letter but not the firm's standard.
Recompute renewal invitation lead times against the host-state statutory period taken from the transposition text.
Reconcile the audit's timeliness result to the operational dashboard and investigate any difference as a reporting-integrity finding.
checklist.done: timing is recomputed for every sampled policy against both the Directive and the firm's standard, and reconciled to operational reporting.

checklist.step: Test the language and host-state add-ons
actions: Confirm each sampled pack is in the official language of the member state of the commitment or has a recorded customer agreement to another language under Art. 23(1).
Check each host-state add-on on the criteria grid appears in the pack - local ombudsman details, prescribed statements, local register wording.
Where a translated pack is tested, obtain a back-translation of the IPID headings and confirm the prescribed wording was not paraphrased.
Attach the translation certificate reference to the workpaper or record its absence.
checklist.done: language compliance and every host-state add-on are tested per sampled pack, with back-translation evidence for translated packs.

checklist.step: Test the delivery proof rather than the system status
actions: For each sampled policy follow the notice-log proof reference to the mail vendor manifest line, e-mail delivery receipt or portal publication record.
Treat a Despatched status with no external proof as a fail on evidence, whatever the system says.
For non-paper delivery check the durable-medium consent and internet-access evidence under Art. 23(5) pre-dated the despatch.
Capture each proof record into the audit file.
checklist.done: every sampled despatch is evidenced by an external proof record and, for electronic delivery, pre-dated consent evidence.

checklist.step: Test the second-line monitoring for reliability
actions: Take Compliance's monthly delivery test and quarterly complaints test workpapers for the period.
Re-perform two of their samples end to end and compare conclusions - where second line passed an item audit fails, the monitoring itself is a finding.
Check second-line exceptions were raised, owned and closed on evidence rather than on assertion.
Rate the reliance that can be placed on second-line monitoring and state it in the report.
checklist.done: second-line monitoring is re-performed on two samples and a stated reliance rating is supported by the comparison.

checklist.step: Quantify the impact of every defect
actions: For each defect type, query the full population for the same condition rather than reporting the sample count alone.
State the number of customers affected, the host states and the period over which the defect ran.
Where the defect concerns pre-contract information, note whether cancellation or withdrawal rights may need restating and hand the analysis to Consumer Affairs.
Have the quantification query reviewed by a second auditor before it enters the report.
checklist.done: each defect carries a population-wide affected-customer count, a date range and a reviewed query behind it.

checklist.step: Rate and agree the issues with management
actions: Rate each issue on the audit scale using the affected-customer count, the article breached and whether it repeats a prior-year finding - repeats are rated High automatically.
Issue the draft report within 30 days of fieldwork close and require management responses within 15 business days.
Reject responses that promise a review without a specific change, an owner and a date.
Record any management disagreement in the report rather than negotiating the finding away.
checklist.done: every issue is rated, responded to with a specific dated action, and any disagreement is recorded in the report.

checklist.step: Report to the audit committee
actions: Present the audit opinion, the issue ratings, affected-customer totals and the reliance rating on second-line monitoring.
Highlight any zero-tolerance breach - missing mandatory disclosure or pack despatched after conclusion - explicitly rather than in an appendix.
Record the committee's directions on remediation pace and on any customer redress or regulator notification question referred to Regulatory Counsel.
Publish the final report to the board portal for the committee record.
checklist.done: the audit committee minute records the opinion, ratings, zero-tolerance breaches and directions, with the report on the board portal.

checklist.step: Follow up the actions to evidenced closure
actions: Track each action to its due date and chase the owner and their executive on the monthly ageing report.
Close an action only after inspecting the evidence - a new template version, a released configuration, a delivered module, a re-run population query showing the defect gone.
Re-test High-rated issues at six months on a fresh sample rather than accepting the fix on paper.
Report any action extended more than once to the audit committee.
checklist.done: every action is closed on inspected evidence, High issues are re-tested at six months and repeat extensions are reported.

checklist.step: File the audit file and hand findings to second line
actions: Complete the audit file - programme, criteria grid, population and sample records, tested packs, recomputations, exception schedules, responses and the signed report.
Apply the 10-year audit retention label and confirm reviewer sign-off is recorded on every workpaper.
Cross-link the issue log to the compliance evidence repository so Compliance can carry the findings into its own monitoring.
Hand the defect quantification to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for the customer remediation decision.
checklist.done: a complete, reviewer-signed, retention-labelled audit file is filed and its findings handed to second line with the impact quantification.

testing.step: Rebuild the audit population independently
actions: Re-run the policy extract for the audit period and selected host states using your own query rather than the audit team's saved one.
Compare the row count and the total premium to the audit population and to the new-business production report.
List any policy class the audit extract silently excluded - broker-bound, embedded partner, mid-term new covers.
Resolve every difference before assessing the audit's conclusions.
testing.done: the audit population is independently rebuilt and reconciled, with any silent exclusion identified.

testing.step: Verify the sample is reproducible from the recorded method
actions: Re-draw the sample from the recorded seed, strata and population size and compare it item by item to the audited sample.
Confirm the mandatory strata were fully taken - all IBIPs, all new host states, all late packs.
Check the sample was locked before fieldwork by comparing the lock timestamp to the first test result timestamp.
Fail the test where the sample cannot be reproduced from the documented method.
testing.done: the sample re-draws identically from the documented method and the lock pre-dates the first test result.

testing.step: Re-perform the content grid on a sub-sample
actions: Select 15 of the audited packs and score them against the criteria grid without reading the audit conclusions first.
Compare your pass/fail to the auditor's on every row and list disagreements with the article and the evidence.
Check that each recorded pass carries the page and paragraph reference the programme requires.
Treat any pass recorded without a reference as untested rather than as compliant.
testing.done: 15 packs are independently re-scored, disagreements are listed by article and unreferenced passes are recorded as untested.

testing.step: Recompute the timing calculations
actions: Recompute despatch minus conclusion for the full sample from the raw timestamps rather than the audit workbook's derived column.
Re-derive the host-state renewal lead times from the transposition text and recompute the renewal timing conclusions.
Compare your late-pack count to the audit's and to the operational dashboard for the same period.
Investigate any three-way difference and record which source is wrong.
testing.done: timing conclusions are recomputed from raw timestamps and reconciled three ways, with the erroneous source identified.

testing.step: Test the criteria grid against the current source texts
actions: Read the criteria grid against the EUR-Lex text of Arts. 17-20, 23 and 29 and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1469 in force during the audit period.
List any testable requirement the grid omitted, particularly Art. 22 cross-selling and Art. 24 ancillary product rules where they applied.
Check each host-state add-on column against the national transposition text rather than the firm's matrix.
Treat an omitted requirement as an audit scope gap and quantify what was not tested.
testing.done: the grid is verified against current source texts and every omitted requirement is listed as a quantified scope gap.

testing.step: Trace defect quantification back to the data
actions: Re-run the population-wide query behind each reported affected-customer count using the same defect definition.
Compare your count to the reported figure and check the date range used matches the period the defect actually ran.
Check the query did not silently drop policies with null host state or null template id, which usually hide the worst cases.
Record the recomputed counts alongside the reported ones in the workpaper.
testing.done: every affected-customer count is recomputed from the underlying data with null handling checked and differences recorded.

testing.step: Test workpaper review and independence
actions: Check every workpaper carries a preparer and a reviewer who are different people and that the review post-dates the preparation.
Confirm no team member on the engagement advised on the disclosure build, the configuration or the second-line monitoring being tested.
Check the report reviewer is the Chief Audit Executive and holds no operational role in distribution or compliance.
Fail the test on any workpaper reviewed by its own preparer.
testing.done: preparer/reviewer separation, review sequencing and team independence are verified for every workpaper.

testing.step: Test issue rating consistency and repeat-finding treatment
actions: Compare each issue's rating to the documented scale using the recomputed affected-customer counts.
Check every finding that repeats a prior-year issue is rated High as the programme requires, and list any that were not.
Check every zero-tolerance breach - missing mandatory element or pack despatched after conclusion - appears in the report body, not an appendix.
List every management response that promises a review rather than a dated, owned change.
testing.done: ratings are tested against the scale and the recomputed counts, repeats are confirmed High and weak responses are listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue for every audit-quality exception - scope gap, unreproducible sample, unreferenced pass, understated impact, weak response accepted.
Assign a root cause (criteria grid built from internal matrix, sample not locked, quantification query defective, rating scale not applied) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date before the next engagement and require the criteria grid to be rebuilt from source where a scope gap is found.
Carry every open issue into the next annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every audit-quality exception has an issue with root cause, owner, a pre-next-engagement date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: State the re-performance agreement rate on the content grid and the timing recomputation and compare to the 2% content defect threshold.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - on whether the audit provides reliable assurance over IDD documentation.
Have the independent reviewer, who performed none of the audited fieldwork, sign the workpaper.
Report the quality assessment to the audit committee alongside the engagement report and file both in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the re-performance agreement rate, a conclusion on assurance reliability and an audit committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the sustainability disclosures that sit on top of IDD distribution - the sustainability-preferences questioning under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 as amended by (EU) 2021/1257, the sustainability factors in the POG target market under (EU) 2017/2358, and the SFDR entity and product disclosures and EIOPA survey returns

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Arts. 2(4), 9 and 14 and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2358 Arts. 5-8 as amended by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/1257 (applicable from 2 August 2022), read with SFDR (EU) 2019/2088 Arts. 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 11, the RTS in Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/1288 and Taxonomy Regulation (EU) 2020/852 Arts. 5-7

In-scope processes.value: IBIP product oversight and governance sustainability target-market setting, the point-of-sale sustainability-preferences question set and matching, SFDR entity website disclosures, pre-contractual and periodic product annexes, the principal adverse impacts statement, and EIOPA and host-NCA sustainability survey responses

Compliance procedure documented.value: Sustainability Disclosure and Survey Procedure - one row per disclosure (Art. 3 policy statement, Art. 4 PAI statement, Art. 6 pre-contractual, Arts. 8/9 product annexes, Art. 11 periodic report, Taxonomy KPIs, EIOPA survey) with its RTS template, data owner, preparer, reviewer, approver and publication location

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual - the SFDR Art. 4 principal adverse impacts statement is published by 30 June each year for the preceding calendar year, Art. 11 periodic product disclosures accompany the annual report, website Art. 3 and Art. 10 disclosures are reviewed and re-dated annually, and EIOPA or host-NCA survey responses are returned by the date stated in the request

Deadline reminders configured.value: Disclosure calendar tasks at 30 June minus 90, 60 and 30 days for the PAI statement, an annual-report-minus-45-days task for the periodic annexes, and a survey intake rule that books preparer, reviewer and approver dates the day a request arrives

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Published disclosure PDFs with publication timestamps, the data extracts and calculation workbooks behind every metric, vendor data files, sign-off records and submitted survey responses, retained 10 years

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missed publication dates, metrics restated after publication, unapproved website changes and survey answers not reconciled to a source extract are logged with root cause, restatement note and owner

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every published sustainability disclosure, every restatement and every EIOPA or NCA survey submission before it leaves the firm

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every sustainability disclosure published or submitted in the reporting year from the disclosure register - website statements, PAI statement, per-product pre-contractual and periodic annexes and survey returns - plus the IBIP population subject to sustainability-preference questioning
